method_sources.A.1.2_A.2.1_A.4.3: SSFR; frozen fact MLP; attention trained on mapping A; replacement with a separately trained memory for mapping B without reader retraining.
method_sources.A.4.5: Standalone CE versus full-value-vector MSE was compared in the book-author language-modeling experiment. Moving that comparison to SSFR is an extension, not an exact replication of the reported approximately 90 percent CE result.

primary_question: When fact memories classify their stored keys successfully, does the standalone training objective affect whether a frozen surrounding reader can use a replacement memory for a new fact mapping?
claim_level: Controlled synthetic behavioral comparison of memory usability and replacement, with targeted interface diagnostics.

accepted_matrix.architecture: One layer and one attention head; no positional encoding; frozen embeddings; identity frozen V/O projections; no attention or MLP residual; unit normalization at the MLP input and final output, following the SSFR paper preset. The SwiGLU fact memory with bias follows the book-author configuration; this differs from the bilinear gated-identity default described for the paper's SSFR GD capacity experiments.
accepted_matrix.formal_final_matrix: Readers trained around CE-A and MSE-A are each evaluated with CE-B and MSE-B; surrounding weights remain fixed during all replacements.
accepted_matrix.interpretation_of_replicates: Three worlds are the independent replication units. Objectives, individual queries, and repeated measurements within a world are paired or nested observations.

necessary_comparisons.name: standalone_exact_keys
necessary_comparisons.purpose: Determine whether the stored facts are available before attributing failure to integration.
necessary_comparisons.measurement: Report fact-candidate accuracy, actual full-vocabulary head accuracy, and value-vector error for both A and B memories.

necessary_comparisons.name: reader_A_on_fresh_A_contexts
necessary_comparisons.purpose: Determine whether each surrounding reader learned to use its original memory on fresh SSFR contexts.
necessary_comparisons.measurement: Evaluate final A accuracy using contexts distinct from the reader training stream. Keep failures in the primary results.

necessary_comparisons.name: two_by_two_reader_memory_cross
necessary_comparisons.purpose: Separate dependence on which memory trained the reader from dependence on which replacement memory is being queried.
necessary_comparisons.measurement: Report all four CE/MSE reader-by-B-memory cells, with shared evaluation contexts and no reader updates. This is more informative than comparing only the two diagonal cells.

necessary_comparisons.name: wrong_A_memory_on_B_labels
necessary_comparisons.purpose: Check whether B accuracy reflects using the replacement mapping instead of retained A behavior.
necessary_comparisons.measurement: Score the unmodified A memory against B labels on the identical B prompts. Report both all keys and the predetermined subset for which A and B labels differ; retain random mapping coincidences.

necessary_comparisons.name: clean_query_through_actual_head
necessary_comparisons.purpose: Separate a memory/head classification failure from failure under the query actually supplied by attention.
necessary_comparisons.measurement: At the query position, replace only the MLP input by its exact stored key and retain the actual MLP, output normalization, and full-vocabulary head. This is an explicitly oracle diagnostic, not autonomous retrieval performance.

competitive_explanations.explanation: One objective has not learned the standalone facts, or one reader has not learned the A task within the budget.
competitive_explanations.design_response: Inspect development learning curves and exact-key/full-head/A-reader performance before freezing the formal matrix. Formal failures remain reported; standalone-correct subsets are secondary and include coverage.
competitive_explanations.remaining_limit: Matched optimizer steps do not establish equally optimized solutions. Fixed-budget differences are not intrinsic impossibility results or general objective rankings.

competitive_explanations.explanation: The apparent integration gap is caused by a different output candidate set.
competitive_explanations.design_response: Official standalone accuracy uses only fact values whereas the Transformer head also includes junk and query tokens. Compare exact-key accuracy under the actual full head before attributing a gap to attention or modular incompatibility.

competitive_explanations.explanation: CE merely creates larger output norms than MSE.
competitive_explanations.design_response: The SSFR final unit normalization cancels positive scalar output rescaling, up to numerical effects. Raw output-norm differences alone cannot explain final top-1 differences in this architecture. Describe output direction and the actual normalized interface instead.
competitive_explanations.remaining_limit: Objective-dependent optimization, angular margins, and responses to imperfect queries can still differ. MSE versus CE does not isolate one of these mechanisms by itself.

competitive_explanations.explanation: The surrounding reader uses fact-specific information or a particular memory's behavior away from its training keys.
competitive_explanations.design_response: Freeze the reader during B replacement; use the two-by-two cross and the clean-query diagnostic. The identity V/O and disabled residuals follow the paper's restricted architecture intended to discourage alternate fact storage.
competitive_explanations.remaining_limit: These restrictions do not prove that all trainable reader computation is fact-independent. Replacement failure alone also combines a changed mapping with a refitted memory; distinguishing these causes completely would require a same-map independent refit control.

competitive_explanations.explanation: Test-aware stopping, different random streams, or unintended training during replacement produces the observed difference.
competitive_explanations.design_response: Do not use B accuracy for model selection or early stopping. Evaluate frozen endpoints, isolate training/evaluation random streams, hash frozen surrounding weights, and verify restore/reload behavior.

development_and_formal_separation.development: The one development world is for checking scoring, optimization sufficiency, and implementation. Adjustments require a recorded reason and must be frozen before the three formal worlds are interpreted as confirmation. Lack of a CE/MSE difference is not a reason to tune for a larger difference.
development_and_formal_separation.formal: Use all three independent worlds and both objectives. Do not select the best B endpoint, discard failures, resample inconvenient mappings, or append training based on formal outcomes while retaining the original fixed-budget interpretation.
development_and_formal_separation.mastery: No universal 100 percent gate is imposed. Report necessary prerequisite accuracies and the extent to which their failures constrain interpretation.

implementation_checks_reviewed: Confirm the resolved SSFR paper settings rather than relying on configuration-class defaults, which differ in positional encoding and normalization.
Confirm CE/MSE refer to the standalone MLP objectives and both reader trainings use the same stated objective.
Confirm attention cannot see the answer token when predicting at Q, despite that token being present later in the generated sequence.
Confirm the clean-query intervention uses the stored key in the actual post-normalization coordinate system.

Confirm A and B memories are trained separately and never initialized from each other's trained weights. Record their initialization seeds; shared initial seeds across maps must be described as paired initialization rather than independent initialization.
Confirm per-objective pairing, full-vocabulary scoring, wrong-map labels, no B-dependent stopping, frozen weights during replacement, exact restoration, and checkpoint reload predictions.

implementation_audit.test_scope: Tiny CPU models; four standalone memories per world each trained for three epochs, two readers each trained for four steps. Two tiny worlds were used to test whether changing B influences A-reader training. No development or formal experiment training was run by this reviewer.
verified: Only Q and K projection weights are trainable; V/O remain identity; embeddings and inserted memory are frozen; interfaces have unit L2 norm and there are no positional encodings or residuals.

Evaluation contexts are balanced over keys, preserve RNG state, are independent of mapping labels, and end at the query token. Training targets align with that query; the future answer is removed before training.
Changing a future answer cannot change earlier query logits, and deleting that answer gives the same query logits.
A constructed example passes fact-only classification while failing the full head, demonstrating that the candidate-set audit distinguishes a real confound.
Standalone normalized full-head scores match an exact-key intervention at the actual reader MLP input through the actual normalization and head.
Evaluation preserves parameter values, RNG state, training/evaluation mode, and hook registration state.
All four reader-by-B-memory scores reproduce after checkpoint reload; wrong-A-on-B uses unchanged A logits with B labels; swapping back restores original parameters and logits exactly.
Changing B's mapping changes fitted B-memory weights while leaving A memories, A-reader final weights, and reader training streams unchanged.
implementation_audit.qualification: A and B memories are fitted separately from the same starting initialization; the implementation and report should call this paired initialization rather than independent starting weights. The clean-query baseline is computed directly from the memory and shared frozen head; its equivalence to the actual hooked reader interface is covered by a test.

relation_to_existing_project.continuous_twohop: Earlier continuous two-hop tests controlled a known value-to-key interface and its errors. This experiment instead trains a surrounding causal attention reader and evaluates replacement use in SSFR; it does not yet test two-hop value-to-key composition.
relation_to_existing_project.architecture_toy: Earlier GQA/hybrid toy models were trained end to end and compared direct versus two-call composition and activation interventions. Here an independently trained, frozen fact memory is the manipulated module, and mapping B is never used to train the surrounding reader.
relation_to_existing_project.P1_P4: Whole-memory replacement is not a constrained shared-parameter update. This experiment does not test the P1/P3 preservation geometry or the P4 gradient-flow rate.

permitted_conclusions: At this fixed scale, architecture, and training budget, quantify original-task learning and no-reader-retraining fact-mapping replacement for each objective.
If exact-key full-head accuracy is high but end-to-end B accuracy is lower, establish a gap between stored-key classification and usability under the reader's supplied queries in this setting.

If the cross-matrix shows an objective-dependent difference, describe a controlled objective effect on reader/memory compatibility; do not identify a unique internal cause without further discriminating evidence.
If both objectives transfer well, report that classification training suffices in this restricted setting; do not treat absence of the anticipated gap as failure or infer universal sufficiency.
unsupported_conclusions: Full-vector MSE is necessary for memory integration, or CE cannot support it.
A universal architecture, optimization, storage-capacity, or two-hop reasoning limit has been established.
These synthetic results identify the cause of knowledge-editing or composition failures in pretrained Qwen, GLM, or Kimi models.
A successful whole-memory replacement demonstrates independent fact updates while preserving an arbitrary surrounding model's other behavior.
Three worlds establish broad statistical robustness or natural-language generalization.
